Awarded through the tariff-based competitive bidding (TBCB) route, the project involves setting up 881 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity. It is targeted for completion by the fourth quarter of 2028, AESL said in a statement on Thursday. The project, named 'Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti', will be executed through a special purpose vehicle, Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd. It is also expected to strengthen Bihar's power transmission network and improve supply reliability. Live Events The project includes four gas-insulated substations at Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transmission lines and transformation infrastructure. Once completed, AESL's transmission network will expand to 30,683 circuit kilometres, while its transformation capacity will increase to 146,585 MVA. The company's transmission capital expenditure pipeline will also rise to around Rs 91,500 crore. "The Pirpainti transmission scheme will create a robust evacuation system for 2,400 MW of generation capacity while strengthening Bihar's transmission backbone," said Kandarp Patel, CEO of Adani Energy Solutions. The project comes amid India's efforts to expand power generation and transmission infrastructure to meet rising electricity demand, requiring investments in both generation capacity and grid connectivity. AESL operates across power transmission, electricity distribution and smart metering. According to the company, it serves around 13 million consumers in Mumbai and Mundra SEZ. bihar_raw_news.title: Adani Energy Solutions wins Bihar transmission project, to generate Rs 500 crore annual ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Adani Energy Solutions wins Bihar transmission project, to generate Rs 500 crore annual tariff revenue ANI | Updated: Nov 19, 2026 17:48 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 19 (ANI): Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL) has secured a power transmission project in Bihar to evacuate 2,400 MW of electricity from Adani Power's upcoming Pirpainti Ultra Super Critical Thermal Power Plant, as per a company statement. According to the company's release, the project was awarded through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism and is scheduled for completion by the last quarter of 2028. “The project, won through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism, will provide annual tariff of Rs ~Rs 500 cr once commissioned,” the company said. As per the release, the project, titled "Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti", will be implemented through the special purpose vehicle (SPV) Vikramshila Power Transmission Limited. Apart from this, the project will not only facilitate evacuation of electricity from the upcoming thermal power plant but also strengthen Bihar's transmission network and improve power supply reliability, the company said. Upon completion, the project will add 881 ckm of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity, taking AESL's total network to 30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA, respectively, the company said. With the addition of the Bihar project , AESL's transmission capital expenditure pipeline now stands at approximately Rs 91,500 crore, according to the release. The project involves constructing four gas-insulated substations (GIS) at Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai, alongside associated transformation infrastructure. It will also include 400 kV transmission lines connecting Pirpainti with Jhanjharpur and Begusarai, and Begusarai with Bakhtiyarpur, besides 220 kV connections and upgrades to existing transmission infrastructure. Kandarp Patel, CEO of Adani Energy Solutions, said, "The Pirpainti transmission scheme will create a robust evacuation system for 2,400 MW of generation capacity while strengthening Bihar's transmission backbone. It will enhance grid reliability and resilience and help the state meet its growing power demand.” "We remain committed to building reliable and efficient transmission infrastructure that supports the country's long-term energy security," he added. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Adani Energy Solutions Wins Bihar Transmission Project With Rs 500 Crore Annual Tariff Potential
bihar_raw_news.content: Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) has won a Bihar transmission project to evacuate electricity from Adani Power’s upcoming 2,400 megawatt (MW) Pirpainti thermal power plant. The scheme is expected to generate an annual tariff of about Rs 500 crore once commissioned, adding a future revenue stream while strengthening the state’s electricity network. Awarded through tariff-based competitive bidding, the project is scheduled for delivery by the last quarter of 2028. It will be implemented through the special purpose vehicle Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd under the scheme titled ‘Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti’. The project will add 881 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and 3,160 megavolt-amperes of transformation capacity. This will take AESL’s transmission portfolio to 30,683 circuit kilometres and transformation capacity to 1,46,585 megavolt-amperes. The line addition represents roughly 3 per cent of the company’s existing network. The infrastructure includes four gas-insulated substations across Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai. Associated 400-kilovolt lines will connect Pirpainti with Jhanjharpur and Begusarai, and Begusarai with Bakhtiyarpur. Additional 220-kilovolt links and modifications to existing lines will support the wider state network. AESL chief executive Kandarp Patel said the scheme would strengthen Bihar’s transmission backbone, improve grid reliability and help meet growing power demand. The award also illustrates that grid investment extends beyond renewable-energy evacuation to thermal generation and state-network reinforcement. Including this project, AESL’s transmission capital expenditure programme stands at about Rs 91,500 crore. This is the broader transmission programme rather than the cost of the Bihar scheme alone. For financial context, consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 27,588.03 crore in FY26. Long-term borrowings, including current maturities, increased to Rs 46,809.95 crore as of March 31, 2026, from Rs 38,223.59 crore a year earlier, making funding discipline important as Construction accelerates. At 3.23 pm on November 19, 2026, AESL shares traded at Rs 1,475.00, down 0.2 per cent from the previous close of Rs 1,478.00. The stock had gained about 50 per cent over one year, against a 1.48 per cent decline in the BSE 500. Separately, Life Insurance Corporation of India’s disclosed stake stood at 3.13 per cent in September 2026, down 0.20 percentage points from June 2026. That ownership change predates the latest announcement. What the Bihar Award Means for AESL’s Growth The Bihar award supports AESL’s long-duration transmission growth, but its contribution lies beyond the immediate earnings horizon. The key distinction is between winning an asset and bringing it into service. Annual tariff potential is not profit, and the eventual earnings contribution will depend on construction costs, financing expenses and operating performance. The project also creates a link between AESL’s network expansion and new thermal generation within the Adani group. Execution deserves particular attention because AESL has already encountered right-of-way constraints on other transmission projects. For this scheme, securing access, completing substations and coordinating readiness with the Pirpainti plant will matter more than the award alone. The development is potentially supportive of future revenue visibility, but the investment case strengthens only as expenditure converts into commissioned assets without material delays

bihar_raw_news.title: Adani Energy Solutions wins Bihar transmission project
bihar_raw_news.content: Adani Energy Solutions wins Bihar transmission project Editor’s Synopsis Project to evacuate 2,400 MW of power from Adani Power’s upcoming Pirpainti Ultra Super Critical Thermal Power Plant and strengthen Bihar’s transmission network Project adds 881 ckm of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to AESL's transmission portfolio Ahmedabad, 19 November 2026 : Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL), India’s leading private sector power transmission and distribution company, today said it has won a transmission project for evacuation of power from the upcoming 2400 MW power plant in Pirpainti, Bihar. The project, won through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism, will provide annual tariff of Rs ~Rs 500 cr once commissioned. The project, titled, “Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti”, will be implemented through the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd. and will be delivered by the last quarter of 2028. Besides evacuation of power from the Pirpainti Power Plant, the project will strengthen the state’s transmission network and enhance supply reliability. “The Pirpainti transmission scheme will create a robust evacuation system for 2,400 MW of generation capacity while strengthening Bihar’s transmission backbone. It will enhance grid reliability and resilience and help the state meet its growing power demand. We remain committed to building reliable and efficient transmission infrastructure that supports the country’s long-term energy security,” said Mr. Kandarp Patel, CEO, Adani Energy Solutions. Upon completion, the project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to AESL’s portfolio, taking it to 30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA. With this project, AESL’s transmission capex now stands at ~Rs 91,500 crore. The project comprises construction of four Gas Insulated Substations (GIS) at Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transformation capacity. The transmission infrastructure will include the 400 kV DCDS Pirpainti-Jhanjharpur, Pirpainti-Begusarai and Begusarai-Bakhtiyarpur lines, as well as the 220 kV DCDS Jhanjharpur-Bethauli and Begusarai-Begusarai Town lines. It will also involve LILO of existing 220 kV and 132 kV transmission lines at Jhanjharpur and construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur GSS. About Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) AESL, part of the Adani portfolio, is a multidimensional organization with presence in various facets of the energy domain, namely power transmission, distribution, smart metering, and cooling solutions. AESL is the country’s largest private transmission company with a cumulative transmission network of 30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA transformation capacity. In its retail electricity distribution business, as on AESL serves approximately 13 million consumers in metropolitan Mumbai and the industrial hub of Mundra SEZ. AESL is ramping up its smart metering business and is on course to become India’s leading smart metering integrator. AESL, with its integrated offering through the expansion of its distribution network through parallel licenses and competitive and tailored retail solutions, including a significant share of green power, is revolutionizing the way energy is delivered to the end consumer. bihar_raw_news.content: ANI Photo | Bihar requests dry port facility expansion beyond Bihta to boost trade Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary stated on November 19 that the state government has requested Union Minister Piyush Goyal and the Ministry of Railways to extend dry port facilities beyond Bihta, particularly near 12 upcoming townships expected to attract investments worth ₹12 lakh crore. Speaking at the ‘Leveraging FTAs Outreach Programme on Boosting Industries, Exports and Business Opportunities’ in Patna, Choudhary highlighted Bihar’s intent to use its international network to access global markets and foster industrial growth. “Bihar Foundation now has international chapters in 31 countries, which we should leverage to tap global markets,” he said. IANS Created On: 19 Nov 2026 3:57 PM IST Comment Share : X Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL) A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Ahmedabad: Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL) on Thursday said it has won a transmission project for evacuation of power from the upcoming 2,400 MW power plant in Pirpainti town in Bhagalpur district, Bihar. Once commissioned, the project, won through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism, will provide annual tariff of Rs 500 crore, said India’s leading private sector power transmission and distribution company in a statement. “The Pirpainti transmission scheme will create a robust evacuation system for 2,400 MW of generation capacity while strengthening Bihar’s transmission backbone. It will enhance grid reliability and resilience and help the state meet its growing power demand,” said Kandarp Patel, CEO, Adani Energy Solutions. “We remain committed to building reliable and efficient transmission infrastructure that supports the country’s long-term energy security,” he added. The project will be implemented through the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd, and will be delivered by the last quarter of 2028. Besides evacuation of power from the Pirpainti Power Plant, the project will strengthen the state’s transmission network and enhance supply reliability, said the Adani Group company. Upon completion, the project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to AESL’s portfolio, taking it to 30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA. With this project, AESL’s transmission capex now stands at Rs 91,500 crore. The project comprises construction of four Gas Insulated Substations (GIS) at Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transformation capacity. The transmission infrastructure will include the 400 kV DCDS Pirpainti-Jhanjharpur, Pirpainti-Begusarai and Begusarai-Bakhtiyarpur lines, as well as the 220 kV DCDS Jhanjharpur-Bethauli and Begusarai-Begusarai Town lines. It will also involve LILO of existing 220 kV and 132 kV transmission lines at Jhanjharpur and construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur GSS. AESL is the country’s largest private transmission company with a cumulative transmission network of 30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA transformation capacity. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced on 13 November 2026 that the newly constructed six-lane Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur Bridge over the Ganga River will be named ‘Nitish Setu’ , after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar . Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the bridge on 21 November 2026. Key Points: Naming of the Bridge: The Bihar government has named the Kachchi Dargah-Raghopur-Bidupur six-lane bridge as ‘Nitish Setu’ in recognition of Nitish Kumar's contribution to the state's development. The announcement was made by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on 13 November 2026. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will dedicate the bridge to the nation during his Bihar visit on 21 November 2026. Geographical Connectivity: The bridge has been constructed across the Ganga River , connecting Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district through Raghopur. It will strengthen connectivity between North and South Bihar . It is expected to reduce traffic congestion on the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu. The main bridge is approximately 9.76 km long , while its total length, including approach roads, is around 19.76 km. Project Background: The foundation stone of the project was laid by Nitish Kumar in August 2015 . The first phase, connecting Kachchi Dargah with Raghopur Diara, was opened to traffic on 23 June 2025 . The project has been developed as a major road infrastructure link for the Patna–Vaishali region. Significance of the Project: Improved connectivity is expected to facilitate movement between Patna and districts of North Bihar. It will support regional economic activities and improve access to markets and public services. It is also expected to provide an alternative route to reduce pressure on existing road bridges across the Ganga. national_raw_news.title: India and Japan to expand maritime security cooperation and joint defence manufacturing
national_raw_news.content: India and Japan have agreed to fast-track defence agreements related to the Unified Complex Radio Antenna or UNICORN stealth naval mast project to strengthen maritime security cooperation and expand joint defence manufacturing following their 2+2 ministerial dialogue in Tokyo. Addressing a joint press briefing alongside External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said the discussions covered a wide range of bilateral and regional issues under the two countries’ Special Strategic and Global Partnership. Mr. Singh said the talks built on the Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation signed in August 2025, as India and Japan prepare to mark 75 years of diplomatic relations in 2027. Highlighting progress in defence ties, he welcomed the first-ever participation of Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft in the bilateral air exercise Veer Guardian 2026 in India and the third India-Japan Defence Industry Forum held in Tokyo on October 13. Both sides also advanced discussions on air and space domain awareness. On maritime security, the two countries agreed to implement their recently signed Memorandum of Arrangement through cooperation in maritime and air domain awareness, search and rescue, and information sharing. They also called for an early conclusion of an agreement allowing reciprocal access to ship repair facilities and agreed to enhance cooperation in mine countermeasure capabilities. Mr. Singh further stressed the need to expedite agreements related to UNICORN, the joint stealth naval mast development initiative, and expand defence industrial collaboration under the ‘Design with Japan, Make in India’ framework, including cooperation in niche, underwater and missile technologies. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said that India-Japan cooperation aims to support a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world, stressing the need for stronger bilateral ties amid growing geopolitical and economic uncertainties. Speaking after the fourth India-Japan 2+2 Foreign and Defence Ministerial Dialogue in Tokyo, Mr. Jaishankar highlighted the two countries’ longstanding friendship and their potential to play a greater role in shaping the global order. He also reaffirmed India’s and Japan’s commitment, alongside their Quad partners, to maintaining a free and open Indo-Pacific. Raising concerns over the growing weaponisation of connectivity, natural resources, services, supply chains and market access, he stressed the need to build resilience and explore alternatives. He particularly highlighted vulnerabilities linked to connectivity and maritime choke points following recent developments in the Gulf. He said, the discussions also covered the changing nature of warfare, including the increasing use of smart weapons and innovative technologies. Mr. Jaishankar said cooperation in these areas would complement the broader India-Japan partnership in innovation and startups.

national_raw_news.title: Govt revises PUC certificate validity, extends renewal intervals for BS-VI vehicles for six months
national_raw_news.content: The Government has revised the validity period of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates for different categories of vehicles. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. According to a gazette notification, the validity of PUC certificates will now depend on the vehicle’s emission standards, category and age. Under the amended rules, vehicles complying with BS-I, BS-II and BS-III emission norms will have a PUC certificate valid for three months, while vehicles complying with BS-IV norms will have a validity of six months. For non-transport vehicles complying with BS-VI emission norms, the certificate will be valid for three years for vehicles up to six years old. While for vehicles more than six years and up to ten years old, the validity will be for one year. For vehicles older than ten years, the validity will be six months. In the case of transport vehicles complying with BS-VI norms, the certificate validity for vehicles up to six years old will be for two years. The validity of the certificate will be one year for vehicles of more than six years and up to ten years old, and six months for vehicles older than ten years. It clarified that if a certificate is renewed within ten days before its expiry, the renewed certificate will take effect from the date of expiry.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi urges industries to make ‘India First’ the foundation of long-term investment...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has asked industries to make ‘India First’ the foundation for every long-term investment decision they take over the next 20 years. He said, this will lead to a self-reliant nation and also open up new opportunities for the growth of their business. Mr Modi was addressing the centenary convention of Industry body FICCI in New Delhi today. He said, over the course of its 100 years, FICCI has witnessed the nation’s industry achieve a great deal. The Prime Minister said, now it is the time to determine what Indian industry can achieve over the next 20 years. He said, over the past 100 years, India’s economy has witnessed many phases. Mr Modi said, people saw the License Quota Raj, the failed experiment of nationalisation and a time in the 21st century when India’s economy was counted among the Fragile Five. The Prime Minister said, however, in the last 12 years, the youth, farmers, workers, and industry leaders have worked hard to transform this situation. He said, today, India is the world’s fastest-growing major economy, projected to grow at around seven per cent. Mr Modi said, last month, India’s goods exports reached nearly 50 billion dollars, its highest-ever monthly goods export. The Prime Minister said, it is due to India’s strong performance that agencies like Moody’s Ratings, S&P Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, the World Bank, and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) are revising the growth forecasts upward. Mr Modi said, the latest World Bank report states that in just 12-13 years, 50 crore Indians have been lifted out of poverty. He said, in the 1970s, when the ‘Garibi Hatao’ slogan was given, India’s population was around 50 crore and poverty could have been eradicated then too. The Prime Minister said, but FICCI is a witness that there was a flaw in policies and unfortunately, a lack of the right intention. He said, when Government worked with the right policies and the right intention, 50 crore poor people came out of poverty in just 12-13 years. Mr Modi said, this shows that the pace and the path on which India is moving today are right, accurate, and hold the guarantee of the nation’s success. Encouraging industry to leverage India’s recent trade agreements, the Prime Minister urged businesses to invest in understanding global customer needs, meeting standards, and building distribution networks. He added that the domestic market should not be the comfort zone, as it must give the confidence to compete in global markets. Emphasising that a nation progresses by honouring farmers, small entrepreneurs, industry, wealth creators, and taxpayers, the Prime Minister listed the pro-business and taxpayer-friendly reforms taken by his government. It includes cutting the basic corporate tax rate from 30 percent in 2014 to 22 percent, exempting income up to 12 lakh rupees to boost purchasing power, simplifying returns and refunds, and lowering GST rates on numerous goods to stimulate demand. Congratulating FICCI on completing 100 years since its inception, Mr Modi said, for an organization to remain consistently vigilant and active for a hundred years, evolving with the changing times and continuing to play its part in the nation’s economic journey is a remarkable achievement.

national_raw_news.title: India records $11.3 bn FPIs in November: CEA Anantha Nageswaran 11 mins ago 4
national_raw_news.content: Chief Economic Adviser, Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran today said that foreign capital is returning sharply to India as oil prices cool below 100 dollars per barrel and the emerging risks regarding AI valuation. Addressing the 65th General Assembly and Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE) in Mumbai, Dr. Nageswaran said India has recorded foreign portfolio inflows of 11.3 billion dollars in just the first 18 days of November. The CEA further underlined that India remains poised to be a big beneficiary in the course of the next financial year as the AI bubble comes down to realistic levels, adding that earlier currency pressures from AI outflows will now likely turn into a source of currency strength. He also highlighted that India has sustained roughly 7 per cent real GDP growth despite global tariff turmoil, supply shocks, and geopolitical conflicts, adding that India has been successful in lifting roughly 500 million people above the 4.20 dollar-a-day moderate poverty line, with rural poverty falling faster than urban in the past decade. While noting that the Indian Government, which had been cautious about trade liberalisation until around 2020, Dr. Nageswaran said that the government has embraced free trade agreements with considerable enthusiasm in the post-pandemic period. He said that India has not only concluded but also operationalised trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand this year alone. He added that a trade agreement with the European Union has also been concluded while trade agreements with the US and Canada are also imminent. Pointing towards India’s strong export performance in the current financial year, the CEA said exports of goods and services stood at around 569 billion dollars from April to October, registering a growth of nearly 17 percent. Talking about the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the CEA flagged five unique challenges – geopolitical fragmentation, China’s manufacturing scale, the energy trilemma, AI-led job shifts, and social media’s impact on youth cognitive skills. To counter these, the CEA said closing technology gaps will buy resilience for India, while agriculture, trade skills, and human-centric services will buy leverage for India.

national_raw_news.title: Banks must focus on building strategy and overcoming technology risks, says RBI Deputy Governor 21 mins ago 8
national_raw_news.content: The Reserve Bank has asked banks to focus on building strategy and overcoming risks, especially technology risks. Speaking at an event organised by Excellence Enablers in Mumbai this morning, RBI Deputy Governor S C Murmu said banks need to invest in technology as well as people to ensure there is no wrongdoing. Emphasizing that banks need to mull over whether they will incentivise volumes or customer outcomes, Mr. Murmu said mis-selling rarely begins at the branch counter; pointing out that it begins with a sales target and a variable pay scale. Clarifying that outsourcing an activity does not mean outsourcing responsibility as the onus for outcomes remains with the banks, Mr. Murmu said banks must rethink their reliance on external vendors for certain tasks. Terming the upcoming transition to Expected Credit Loss – ECL framework as a significant milestone, Mr. Murmu said banks will have to provide for losses they expect and not just for losses already incurred. Stating that the system will be shifting to principles based approach, the RBI Deputy Governor said the remaining Basel-III standards will also take effect. With artificial intelligence-based models now driving parts of credit, collections and fraud detection systems, Mr. Murmu underlined that bank boards need to ensure that decisioning is explainable, fair and accountable. He also said that risks from climate change or cyberattacks may not have an immediate impact, but the dent will show up in the loan book sooner or later.

national_raw_news.title: Odisha evacuates 72,000 people as severe Cyclone Akvan approaches coast 4 hours ago 85
national_raw_news.content: Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the west-central Bay of Bengal is moving north-northwestwards and is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to the east of Gopalpur, by noon tomorrow. The system is expected to cross the coast with wind speeds of 90 to 100 kilometres per hour, gusting up to 110 kilometres per hour. The India Meteorological Department has issued a red warning for extremely heavy rainfall in Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Puri, Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara districts. Meanwhile, Odisha Government has intensified its preparedness to tackle the cyclone. Chief Secretary Anu Garg, briefing the media at the state-level control room in Bhubaneswar today, said nearly 72,000 people have been evacuated to safer locations. Around 7,900 cyclone shelters have been kept ready, and special arrangements have been made for pregnant women and people living in vulnerable hilly areas. Sixty ODRAF teams, 14 NDRF teams and 131 fire service teams have been deployed across vulnerable districts. Earlier yesterday, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed the cyclone preparedness and directed officials to ensure zero casualties. He asked all departments to remain on high alert and ensure timely evacuation and relief measures. The state government has appealed to people to follow official advisories and cooperate with the administration.

national_raw_news.title: Prataprao Jadhav reviews expansion plans of National Institute of Unani Medicine, calls for timely implementation
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush Prataprao Jadhav on Wednesday chaired the 13th Governing Body meeting of the National Institute of Unani Medicine (NIUM) at Kartavya Bhawan-I in New Delhi, reviewing the institute’s ongoing activities and proposed expansion plans. Emphasising NIUM’s role in advancing Unani education, research and healthcare, Jadhav said the institute currently has 71 students across 10 postgraduate departments. Its proposed expansion includes the introduction of five additional postgraduate departments, 35 more seats and a Department of Integrative and Translational Research. Second campus planned at Ghaziabad The Minister also reviewed plans for NIUM’s second campus at Ghaziabad, near Delhi. The proposed campus will include a 200-bed referral hospital, postgraduate education facilities and research infrastructure. Welcoming the proposal to allocate 24 seats to foreign students within the institute’s existing intake capacity, Jadhav said the initiative would strengthen international academic engagement and reflect the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (the world is one family). Minister stresses accountability and public service Outlining his expectations from the institute, Jadhav identified three priorities: timeliness, accountability and service. He called for pending matters to be addressed promptly and directed that clear timelines and responsibilities be assigned to every project to ensure effective implementation. He also emphasised that healthcare services and treatments developed by NIUM should reach all sections of society, particularly the economically disadvantaged. Focus on institutional development During the meeting, NIUM Director Prof. Saiyad Shah Alam welcomed the Union Minister and the Secretary of the Ministry of Ayush. He also presented an overview of the institute’s activities, achievements and proposed initiatives. The meeting was attended by Ayush Secretary Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha; Additional Secretary and Financial Adviser Hoyeeda Abbas; Karnataka Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Finance, Ritesh Kumar Singh; Advisor (Unani), Ministry of Ayush, Dr M.A. Qasmi; President of the Board of Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa, Prof. Asim Ali Khan; and Director General of the Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), Dr N. Zaheer Ahmed, among other senior officials. The meeting concluded with an emphasis on strengthening institutional governance, ensuring the effective implementation of approved initiatives and improving coordination among stakeholders to support NIUM’s future development. (PIB)

national_raw_news.title: India, Burkina Faso explore cooperation in traditional medicine, medicinal plant conservation
national_raw_news.content: India and Burkina Faso on Wednesday discussed expanding cooperation in traditional medicine, medicinal plant conservation, Yoga and wellness programmes, with Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush Prataprao Jadhav expressing India’s readiness to share its expertise and support the West African country’s initiatives in the sector. Jadhav held a meeting with a delegation from Burkina Faso led by Roger Baro, Minister and Special Adviser to the President of Burkina Faso, in New Delhi. The delegation is visiting India from November 17 to 25, with a focus on traditional medicine and engagement with Ayush institutions. During the meeting, Jadhav said India attaches considerable importance to its bilateral relations with Burkina Faso and is keen to strengthen the partnership. He noted that both countries have a rich heritage of traditional medicines and indigenous healthcare practices, providing a strong foundation for collaboration. Focus on medicinal plant conservation and research Jadhav said he had learnt that Burkina Faso President Captain Ibrahim Traore had expressed interest in India’s support for the conservation and sustainable development of the country’s traditional medicinal plants. India is willing to share its experience and expertise in herbal medicine standardisation, quality assurance, pharmacopoeial standards and regulatory frameworks, the Minister said. He also welcomed institutional partnerships between Indian Ayush institutions and relevant traditional medicine institutions in Burkina Faso. Highlighting the potential for a flagship bilateral initiative, he proposed an India-Burkina Faso project on the conservation and sustainable development of traditional plants, involving India’s National Medicinal Plants Board and relevant institutions in Burkina Faso. MoU and cooperation in Yoga and wellness The Minister said India is keen to support the promotion of Yoga and Ayush-based wellness programmes in Burkina Faso. The two countries could also explore signing a Memorandum of Understanding between India’s Ministry of Ayush and Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Health to establish an institutional framework for cooperation. He welcomed Burkina Faso’s participation in future World Health Organization (WHO) Global Summits on Traditional Medicine and programmes organised by the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat. As an immediate step, Jadhav suggested that both sides identify nodal officers to take the proposals forward and work out specific areas of collaboration. India highlights development partnership and capacity building Reaffirming India’s commitment to South-South Cooperation and its engagement through platforms such as the G20 and BRICS, Jadhav said India supports Burkina Faso in achieving its development goals. He emphasised that India’s development partnership is guided by the needs and priorities identified by the Government of Burkina Faso. He also highlighted India’s contribution to capacity building through training and scholarship programmes, including the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme, the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) and the PCFD course. More than 250 Burkinabe nationals have benefited from these initiatives in recent years. Jadhav also acknowledged the contribution of the Indian community in Burkina Faso to the country’s socio-economic development and expressed India’s expectation of continued support from the Burkinabe government in ensuring the community’s safety and security. He said India remains committed to advancing traditional medicine cooperation through knowledge exchange, institutional collaboration and capacity building, and wished the visiting delegation a productive visit. Senior officials from both sides attend meeting The Burkina Faso delegation included Prof. Rakissida Alfred Ouedraogo, Special Ministerial Advisor for Higher Education and Health Issues; Dr Mariam Sawadogo/Bagayan, Director of Traditional and Alternative Medicine at the Ministry of Health; Prof. Aminata Pagnimdebsom Nacoulma, a pharmacognosy specialist and lecturer-researcher at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University; and Dr Hyacinthe Bonkoungou, Director of the Center for Traditional Medicine and Integrated Care. The Burkina Faso Embassy was represented by Ambassador Some Désiré Boniface, Deputy Chief of Mission Zingué-ouattara Didier Christian and interpreter Ouoba Joël. India’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso O.P. Meena and Kailash Bhatt, Under Secretary (Central and West Africa) in the Ministry of External Affairs, also attended. Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, and senior officials of the Ministry were present. The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of India and Burkina Faso to deepen cooperation in traditional medicine and strengthen institutional ties between their respective healthcare and research organisations. (PIB)

Manipur registers 317 cases under NDPS Act in 2026: NCB official November 19, 2026 Correspondent IMPHAL, NOV 18: As many as 441 persons were arrested as law enforcing agencies in Manipur registered a total of 317 cases during the current year till October compared to 284 NDPS cases with 349 arrests in the previous year 2025, an official of the Narcotic Control Bureau (NCB), Imphal Zonal Unit. The superintendent of NCB added that a total of 269 persons arrested in different NDPS cases were currently in jail and 166 on bail. While sharing the data, Aram Anth, the superintendent of NCB, Imphal Zonal Unit revealed the challenges being faced by law enforcing agencies in dealing with the drug trafficking in the state, particularly cross border trafficking. He was speaking as a resource person at a one-day media workshop (Varta) hosted by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Regional Office, Imphal in Thoubal district today. He said that as Manipur shares an international border with Myanmar, close to the Golden Triangle region, the region faces a persistent drug trafficking challenge. Long borders and difficult terrain made it a challenging task for the law enforcing agencies in dealing with the menace, he said, before adding that lasting results need community support and inter-agency coordination. He said that rampant poppy cultivation practices in the hill region of the state were other challenges in the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan (NMBA), a nationwide campaign launched by the Central government, in the state. citing the impact of the illicit practice on the environment, he said, “Environmental perspective-ecological disaster, soil erosion, landslides, loss of flora and fauna, increases in crime rate, and affect economy/production were the impact of the illicit practice.” Launched on 15 August 2020, the NMBA is a nationwide people’s movement against substance abuse. The main objective of the campaign is building India a drug-free nation ahead of the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision. The PIB, Regional Office, Imphal, organised the one-day media workshop (Varta) for the journalists and media professionals in Thoubal, Kakching and Chandel districts. national_raw_news.title: Beyond the big screen: IFFI 2026 to showcase five films about filmmaking - Mathrubhumi English
national_raw_news.content: IFFI 2026 Introduces 'Films About Films' Section With Five International Movies | Mathrubhumi English Home page » Movies & Music » News » IFFI 2026 Beyond the big screen: IFFI 2026 to showcase five films about filmmaking Published By: Salma Sulthana Last Updated: 19 November 2026, 11:38 AM IST Follow us on Photo: IMDb, PIB What happens behind the camera can sometimes be as fascinating as what unfolds on screen. The struggles of a filmmaker, an actor's relationship with a character, or even a film that never got made can reveal a great deal about the world of cinema. The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is set to explore these lesser-known stories through a new section titled 'Films About Films'. Making its debut at this year's festival, the section will feature five international films that look at cinema from a different perspective. Rather than focusing only on the stories told through films, the selection takes audiences into the lives, creative journeys and challenges of the people who make them. The initiative is part of IFFI 2026's theme, 'Stories Without Borders'. The festival organisers said the new section was introduced following suggestions from established filmmakers, with the aim of giving greater attention to the art and craft of filmmaking. The five-film selection brings together productions from 10 countries, including the UK, the US, Russia, Georgia, Estonia, Turkey, Switzerland, France, Germany and Italy. From a portrait of a legendary director to the story of a forgotten Hollywood screenplay, the line-up covers different aspects of cinema and its history. David lean's life and legacy The section opens with a documentary on David Lean, the celebrated filmmaker behind classics such as ‘The Bridge on the River Kwai’, ‘Lawrence of Arabia’ and ‘Doctor Zhivago’. Directed by Barnaby Thompson, ‘Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean’ explores the director's career, his ambitious approach to filmmaking and the vision that helped shape some of cinema's most memorable works. The 105-minute English-language documentary also looks beyond his professional achievements to examine the personal difficulties and creative challenges that accompanied his journey. It offers an opportunity to revisit the work of a filmmaker whose influence continues to be felt across generations. A family story from Georgia Moving away from the life of a filmmaker, Raul Geidarov's ‘Sidney Lumet's Birthday’ tells a more personal story about family, childhood and unexpected change. The Russian-language film follows 17-year-old Dato, a Georgian boy who lives with his grandmother. Their quiet existence is shaped by the absence of several family members, until his mother suddenly returns after being away for a long time. Her arrival changes the rhythm of their lives and brings unresolved emotions to the surface. Through Dato's experiences, the film explores family bonds, growing up and the difficulties of holding on to one's humanity during uncertain times. national_raw_news.content: World Heritage Week: ASI monuments to offer free entry on Thursday | Mathrubhumi English Home page » Lifestyle » Travel » World Heritage Week World Heritage Week: ASI monuments to offer free entry on Thursday # PTI Last Updated: 19 November 2026, 09:29 AM IST Follow us on New Delhi: Entry to Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)-protected monuments across the country will be free on Thursday to mark the opening day of World Heritage Week, a senior official said. World Heritage Week is observed every year from November 19-25. "Celebrate India's rich heritage! On 19th November 2026, mark World Heritage Week with FREE ENTRY to all @ASIGoI monuments! Explore our magnificent monuments, discover stories of our glorious past, and experience the timeless legacy of India's cultural heritage," PIB Culture posted on X. The official said the waiver of tickets applies only on November 19 for now. The ASI protects more than 3,800 monuments and sites across the country, of which 143 are ticketed. These include the Taj Mahal in Agra and the Red Fort and Qutub Minar in Delhi. (This story has not been edited by Mathrubhumi and is published from a syndicated feed.)
